$comment: Target profile for common St John's wort, an introduced Eurasian perennial and a provincially regulated noxious weed in BC. Same dry, disturbed, low-elevation niche as mullein, but on somewhat less sparse ground: it forms patches in dry grassland and open forest rather than needing bare soil.
habitat_note: Introduced; a regulated noxious weed in BC (also called Klamath weed). Dry, sunny, disturbed ground in the low valleys: roadsides, rangeland, dry grassy openings and open pine / Douglas-fir forest. Flowers around midsummer (late June to August). The native western St John's wort (H. scouleri) is a different plant of moist montane meadows.

observations.$comment: 43 AOI records. H. scouleri (and the small H. anagalloides) grow in wet meadows and seeps, the opposite of the target's habitat, so their records are down-weighted.

elevation_m.$comment: Records: p05 436 m, median 560 m, p95 1080 m.

ndvi.$comment: Dry grassy ground: higher floor and ceiling than mullein, since it grows in turf rather than on bare gravel.

logging.$comment: Neutral: a disturbance follower that spreads along skid roads and into cut-over dry forest.
